desk.observations: The fitted asset (B) successfully replicates the rigid geometry of the design (A), including the rectangular footprint, the three-drawer pedestal on the left, and the open leg space on the right. The grey-green military furniture style is consistent across both images, with a matte finish and clean, untextured surfaces. The silhouette of the top surface, including the raised back edge, is accurately maintained in the fit. The drawer handles in the fit are simplified to flat, horizontal bars, which is a reasonable manufacturing interpretation of the design's hardware.
defects: The design (A) features a distinct metallic trim or bevel along the front edge of the top surface, which is missing in the fitted asset (B).
The design (A) shows a small, dark rectangular opening or cutout on the right side panel, which is not present in the fit (B).
The rivets or fasteners visible on the side panels in the design are less prominent or absent in the fit.
fixes: Add a metallic trim or bevel to the front edge of the top surface in the fitted asset to match the design.
Include the small rectangular opening or cutout on the right side panel if it is a functional feature (e.g., for cable management).
Enhance the visibility of rivets or fasteners on the side panels to better match the military style of the design.

observations: The fitted asset (D) is an excellent match for the design (C), preserving the circular top, central pedestal, and circular base.
The proportions of the table, including the height of the pedestal and the diameter of the top and base, are consistent between the design and the fit.
The grey-green color and matte finish are identical in both images, maintaining the clean, rigid geometry style.
The rivets around the edge of the top and base are present in both the design and the fit, contributing to the military furniture aesthetic.
defects: The design (C) shows a slightly more pronounced bevel on the edge of the top surface, which is less visible in the fit (D).
The central pedestal in the design (C) appears to have a slightly different taper or profile compared to the fit (D), though this is a minor difference.
fixes: Increase the visibility of the bevel on the edge of the top surface in the fitted asset to match the design.
Adjust the taper or profile of the central pedestal in the fitted asset to more closely match the design.
